user_fraud_transactions = COUNT(IsFraud=1) over all of the user's transactions (go_user_behavior_metrics.sql:11, no date bound), joined by UserID only (go_predictive_model_features.sql:23,28), so it counts the row's own label and later frauds at the transaction's TransactionDate (README.MD:57-58). Same mechanism as #3.

merchant_fraud_transactions = COUNT(IsFraud=1) over all of the merchant's transactions (go_merchant_risk_assessment.sql:10, no date bound), joined by MerchantID only (go_predictive_model_features.sql:24,29), so it includes the row's own label and future frauds. Same mechanism as #2.

The project's cutoff is 2017-03-01 (stg_members.sql:19-23) and the label is renewal within 30 days of a March-2017 expiry (docs/0-glossary.md:22), but int_transaction_features.sql:5-29 aggregates every transaction through 2017-03 (docs/1-data.md:47), including post-expiry renewals, which are the outcome itself (docs/1-data.md:110).

int_user_log_features.sql aggregates all of user_logs_v2, which is March 2017 only (docs/1-data.md:48-50), so every row postdates the 2017-03-01 reference date (stg_members.sql:23) and overlaps each user's expiry/renewal window. The leak is real by availability even though the docs report little label signal in it (docs/1-data.md:100).

ROW_NUMBER ... ORDER BY transaction_date DESC with rn=1 (int_transaction_features.sql:13,57) picks the latest transaction in the unbounded history, which can be a March renewal after the 2017-03-01 cutoff, feeding last_auto_renew/last_cancel/days_until_expiry. Same root cause as #3 (missing time bound), not a separate leak.

stg_transactions.sql:8-32 only reads and dedupes bronze_transactions, which is the label spine itself (one row per transaction, prediction time = its own event_time); no other temporal table is joined, so no future rows enter.

txn_count_1h frame is RANGE BETWEEN 1h PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING on event_time_unix (int_velocity_features.sql:18), so it sees only strictly earlier transactions of the same user (docs/architecture.md:55-57).
txn_count_24h frame ends at 1 PRECEDING (int_velocity_features.sql:24), so it sees only strictly earlier transactions; same pattern as #2/#4.
txn_count_7d frame ends at 1 PRECEDING (int_velocity_features.sql:30), so it sees only strictly earlier transactions; same pattern as #2/#3.

ROW_NUMBER partitioned by transaction_id, ordered by _ingested_at (stg_transactions.sql:14-16), keeps the first-ingested copy of the same transaction (Kafka redelivery dedupe). No other transaction's data, and no later-event information, enters the row.

total_amount_1h frame ends at 1 PRECEDING (int_spend_pattern_features.sql:18), so it uses only earlier transactions; the current amount enters only via the explicit ratio, which is known at scoring time.
total_amount_24h frame ends at 1 PRECEDING (int_spend_pattern_features.sql:24), so it uses past rows only; same pattern as #6-#11.
avg_amount_24h frame ends at 1 PRECEDING (int_spend_pattern_features.sql:30), so it uses past rows only; same pattern as #6-#11.
max_amount_24h frame ends at 1 PRECEDING (int_spend_pattern_features.sql:36), so it uses past rows only; same pattern as #6-#11.
min_amount_24h frame ends at 1 PRECEDING (int_spend_pattern_features.sql:42), so it uses past rows only; same pattern as #6-#11.
max_amount_7d frame ends at 1 PRECEDING (int_spend_pattern_features.sql:48), so it uses past rows only; same pattern as #6-#10.
